lessons.title: Map an argument
lessons.scenario: label a passage's claim, evidence, qualification, and conclusion, each with a text cue.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Map an argument”?
flashcards.answer: label a passage's claim, evidence, qualification, and conclusion, each with a text cue.

assessment: all four functions are located and the qualification is not mistaken for a refutation.

lessons.title: Follow cohesion and scope
lessons.scenario: trace two reference or connective links and identify the scope of a claim.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Follow cohesion and scope”?
flashcards.answer: trace two reference or connective links and identify the scope of a claim.

assessment: both links are accurate and no broader population or causal claim is invented.

lessons.title: Write an analytical summary
lessons.scenario: write a 70–90-word summary retaining evidence, limitation, and implication.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Write an analytical summary”?
flashcards.answer: write a 70–90-word summary retaining evidence, limitation, and implication.

assessment: includes all three required relations and makes no unsupported causal claim.
C1-T-U01 transfer.

lessons.title: Plan for a decision reader
lessons.scenario: organize a report note around a decision question, evidence, limitation, recommendation, and next check.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Plan for a decision reader”?
flashcards.answer: organize a report note around a decision question, evidence, limitation, recommendation, and next check.

assessment: all five functions appear in a logical order and the recommendation remains limited.

lessons.title: Edit agency and register
lessons.scenario: revise nominalized or passive wording when it hides a relevant actor, without making the tone less professional.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Edit agency and register”?
flashcards.answer: revise nominalized or passive wording when it hides a relevant actor, without making the tone less professional.

assessment: actor and meaning are preserved; tone is direct, not inflated.
C1-T-U02 language item.

lessons.title: Draft an evidence-based note
lessons.scenario: produce a 70–100-word manager note including evidence, limitation, and action.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Draft an evidence-based note”?
flashcards.answer: produce a 70–100-word manager note including evidence, limitation, and action.

assessment: all three elements are present and the guide is not credited with an effect that may also come from demonstrations.
C1-T-U02 transfer.

lessons.title: Build a spoken argument map
lessons.scenario: plan a short talk with claim, evidence, limitation, and decision rule.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Build a spoken argument map”?
flashcards.answer: plan a short talk with claim, evidence, limitation, and decision rule.

assessment: no evidence point is used to prove an unmeasured outcome.

lessons.title: Make relations audible
lessons.scenario: use signposting and pausing to make two reasoning relations clear in a spoken explanation.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Make relations audible”?
flashcards.answer: use signposting and pausing to make two reasoning relations clear in a spoken explanation.

assessment: listener identifies the intended relation without seeing the notes.

lessons.title: Respond and repair
lessons.scenario: answer a challenge question relevantly and clarify one ambiguous term.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Respond and repair”?
flashcards.answer: answer a challenge question relevantly and clarify one ambiguous term.

assessment: direct response, accurate qualification, and successful clarification/repair.
C1-T-U03 transfer.

lessons.title: Infer stance from cues
lessons.scenario: support a stance inference with two wording/context cues and label it as inference.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Infer stance from cues”?
flashcards.answer: support a stance inference with two wording/context cues and label it as inference.

assessment: two cues cited; no inferred emotion is stated as fact.

lessons.title: Interpret irony cautiously
lessons.scenario: compare a literal and a plausible ironic reading and state what remains uncertain.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Interpret irony cautiously”?
flashcards.answer: compare a literal and a plausible ironic reading and state what remains uncertain.

assessment: the challenge is recognized while hostility/sarcasm is not assumed.

lessons.title: Paraphrase implication
lessons.scenario: produce a neutral paraphrase and a clearly labeled inference from the same input.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Paraphrase implication”?
flashcards.answer: produce a neutral paraphrase and a clearly labeled inference from the same input.

assessment: explicit content and inference remain distinct and cue-supported.
C1-T-U04 transfer.

lessons.title: Compare methods and constructs
lessons.scenario: state what two sources measure and whether they support a common outcome claim.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Compare methods and constructs”?
flashcards.answer: state what two sources measure and whether they support a common outcome claim.

assessment: no learning-effect claim is inferred from preference or tutor views alone.

lessons.title: Synthesize sources and communicate uncertainty
lessons.scenario: read aloud: “Both reports suggest that schedule flexibility affects people differently. One emphasizes commute experience; the other highlights coordination. A policy may therefore need a shared collaboration window, but the evidence does not establish a single best arrangement.”

flashcards.question: Can either source prove that flexible schedules improve productivity?
flashcards.answer: self-reported commute stress; difficulty collaborating without shared hours; no, neither measures productivity causally

assessment: 0–2 each for accurate attribution, synthesis, qualification, and audience clarity. Success: 6/8 and no misrepresentation. Teacher checks paraphrase and language use.
name one focus of each report and the policy implication.

lessons.title: Synthesize and qualify
lessons.scenario: write a 70–100-word synthesis that attributes both sources, identifies one shared theme and one difference, and proposes no unsupported conclusion.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Synthesize and qualify”?
flashcards.answer: write a 70–100-word synthesis that attributes both sources, identifies one shared theme and one difference, and proposes no unsupported conclusion.

assessment: attribution and distinction are accurate; no causal outcome is invented.
C1-T-U05 transfer.

lessons.title: Listen for interests
lessons.scenario: distinguish a stakeholder's stated position from the interest or constraint it may represent.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Listen for interests”?
flashcards.answer: distinguish a stakeholder's stated position from the interest or constraint it may represent.

assessment: label proposals as proposals and do not assign motives as facts.

lessons.title: Negotiate conditional options
lessons.scenario: formulate an option with a clear condition and confirm whether it is accepted.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Negotiate conditional options”?
flashcards.answer: formulate an option with a clear condition and confirm whether it is accepted.

assessment: every condition is retained and no discussion is reported as consensus.

lessons.title: Mediate the decision
lessons.scenario: relay the decision and one unresolved issue to a new audience without altering either.

flashcards.question: What is the goal of “Mediate the decision”?
flashcards.answer: relay the decision and one unresolved issue to a new audience without altering either.

assessment: condition, common ground, and unresolved matter are all accurately represented.
C1-T-U06 transfer.
